subject: Ventura go-live: dependency on request-level audit + acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@venturahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@venturahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-23 09:05 AM PST
Subject: Feature alignment for Ventura go-live — milestone dependency?

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're lining up procurement and the legal review and have a hard activation target of 2027-01-15 for our pilot. As we walked through the mutual action plan, one item keeps coming up with our security and audit teams: they need per-request auditability and a deterministic export of inference request traces (user id, model variant, tokens, and route id) for 90 days.

We understand Redwood's general telemetry posture, but for our compliance signoff the ask is specific: an exportable, signed audit artifact that we can drop into our SIEM. This feels like a product dependency rather than a configuration toggle. Can you confirm whether this is in scope for inclusion ahead of our go-live? If not, what scoping or timeline should we expect?

I've attached the latest Mutual Action Plan and a gap matrix we've sketched. If this is a product-level change, we'll need to know by Dec 6 to keep procurement on schedule.

Appreciate the help — Sophie

--
Sophie Lane
Director, Platform Security
Ventura Health
Attachment: Ventura_Mutual_Action_Plan_v3.pdf
Attachment: feature_gap_matrix.xlsx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@venturahealth.com>
Cc: Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@venturahealth.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-23 10:20 AM PST
Subject: Re: Feature alignment for Ventura go-live — milestone dependency?

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear writeup and the MAP. Looping in Product (Laura), Eng (Ben) and CS (Monica) so we can triage the ask quickly.

Short answer: we can likely cover something acceptable for your procurement window, but we need to (1) agree the acceptance criteria that will satisfy your auditors, and (2) define a scoped rollout (full, canary, or export-only) we can deliver before Jan 15.

Requests for the team:
- Laura: can you review the attached gap matrix and propose a minimal acceptance criteria set (fields + retention + signed artifact) that would be considered "compliant" by security?
- Ben: high-level feasibility and rough ETA if scoped to an export + signed audit artifact (no UI) vs full request-level trace streaming into your SIEM.
- Monica: prepare a customer-facing mitigation/temporary workflow we can offer if we need more time (e.g., scheduled export + manual handoff).

Sophie, we'll follow up with a short decision checklist by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0192

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@venturahealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-24 02:05 PM PST
Subject: Re: Feature alignment for Ventura go-live — milestone dependency?

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed the gap matrix and sketched a minimal acceptance criteria that I think will get your auditors to green:
- export rows: timestamp (UTC), request_id, user_id (hashed opt), model_id, model_variant, route_id, prompt_length, response_length, token_counts, top-level latency
- artifacts exported as signed daily bundles (GZIP + detached signature) delivered to a secure S3 location or via SFTP
- 90-day retention policy with on-demand historical bundle retrieval API
- a simple schema and a signed checksum per bundle to prove integrity

Implementation options:
1) Export-only (fast): batch daily bundles + signature. Low eng effort, can be delivered as a config/ops feature.
2) Streaming (medium): near-real-time export to SIEM — more engineering + operational cost, needs routing hooks and higher SLA testing.
3) Integrated audit UI (long): built into Console with search and replay — not feasible before Jan.

Given your timeline, the Export-only approach (1) seems realistic. Ben — do you agree on an ETA if we scope to Option 1 and provide schema + signed bundle? Rough sizing please (days/sprints). Also, Sophie — can you confirm that hashed user_id is acceptable for your compliance team (they said PII redaction is required).

Linking the HubSpot ticket here: https://hubspot.company/record/VENT-2026-1123

Laura Bennett
Senior PM, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@venturahealth.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-25 08:15 AM PST
Subject: Re: Feature alignment for Ventura go-live — milestone dependency?

Laura — agree with the export-only path as the pragmatic approach to meet a tight deadline. Quick notes from engineering feasibility triage: 
- Work required: add export pipeline, bundle signing (we can re-use existing key rotation flow + HMAC), retention enforcement, and an API for bundle listing + retrieval.
- Rough estimate: 3-5 engineering sprints (2-week sprints) to build, test, and harden if we include automated signing and retrieval API. If we scope to a manual handoff (daily bundle dropped to a pre-provisioned S3 and we do the signature step via ops script), we can compress to 2 sprints for an MVP (engineering + ops support).
- Blocking questions: which signing approach (HMAC vs RSA detached signature) does Ventura's security prefer? Also need S3/SFTP destination details and an internal wallet/key approval for one-time signing.

Proposed near-term plan:
- MVP (2 sprints): nightly export bundles + ops-run signature, manual S3 drop + scripted retrieval endpoint.
- Follow-up (3-4 sprints): automate signing, add retrieval API, integrate retention policy.

Monica, I'll pair with you on runbook and escalations. Jordan — recommend we get a written scope confirmation from Ventura (accepts hashed user_id, export-only ok, signing format) so we can lock dates for sprint planning.

Ben Carter
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachment: implementation_notes.md

From: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@venturahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@venturahealth.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-25 11:40 AM PST
Subject: Re: Feature alignment for Ventura go-live — milestone dependency?

Thanks everyone — that breakdown is very helpful. Ventura's security team reviewed and confirms: hashed user_id + RSA detached signature on bundles is preferred. The S3 bucket route is acceptable; we'll provide bucket write credentials and an endpoint contact by Nov 30. We also accept the Export-only MVP approach provided Redwood commits in writing to the Jan 15 pilot target and a follow-up schedule for automation.

Action items we need from Redwood by EOD Dec 6:
- A scope confirmation email listing fields, retention, signature type, and delivery method.
- Target sprint dates (start of work and expected MVP delivery date).
- Any procurement language we need to add to the SOW to reflect this dependency.

If you can send the scope confirmation and an intake ticket (HubSpot ID) we can circulate internally and keep procurement on schedule. Appreciate the flexibility — Sophie
